title: Zero Dollars: 10 Hangs That Cost Nothing
description: Discover the best spots around Appalachian State University for social activities and relaxation that require no admission or purchase, from campus landmarks to scenic mountain overlooks.

cards.entity_name: Turchin Center for the Visual Arts
cards.title: Browse Contemporary Art Galleries
cards.subtitle: King Street Art Hub
cards.notes: Explore six galleries of contemporary art with rotating exhibitions. Admission is always free for students and the public; check for Friday evening exhibition celebrations.
cards.short_summary: A university-run visual arts center featuring local and international contemporary works with free admission.
cards.evidence_claim: Admission to the center is always free. The Turchin Center for the Visual Arts in Boone, North Carolina welcomes visitors to experience the arts... Admission is always FREE.
cards.source_title: Visit | Turchin Center for the Visual Arts
cards.access_notes: Open Tuesday-Thursday and Saturday 10am-6pm, Friday 12pm-8pm. Closed Sundays, Mondays, and during home football games.

cards.title: Hammock and Socialize on the Quad
cards.subtitle: The Heart of Campus
cards.notes: Join the campus community on this central green space for hammocking, slacklining, or people-watching. It is the primary hub for student-led events and outdoor lounging.
cards.short_summary: The central grassy quad of App State, serving as the main social gathering point for outdoor activities.
cards.evidence_claim: Sanford Mall is the name of a green area of campus that hosts all sorts of outdoor booths... It is also where students meet to practice rope walking or to swing or just hang out.
cards.access_notes: Public outdoor space available 24/7; most active during daylight hours between classes.

cards.title: Study in the 24-Hour Commons
cards.subtitle: Late Night Study Hub
cards.notes: Utilize five floors of study space, including quiet zones and group rooms. Students have 24/5 access with an AppCard; community members are welcome during daylight hours.
cards.short_summary: The main university library offering extensive study spaces, technology resources, and 24-hour access for students.
cards.evidence_claim: Belk Library and Information Commons... Open 24 hours a day, Sunday - Thursday... After midnight, Belk Library is only open to students, faculty, and staff.
cards.access_notes: Open 24 hours Sunday-Thursday for students. Public access ends at midnight. AppCard required for late-night entry.

cards.title: Paint the Expression Tunnels
cards.subtitle: Under Rivers Street
cards.notes: Grab a can of spray paint and add your own art to the walls of the tunnels connecting campus. This is the only designated area where graffiti is officially encouraged.
cards.short_summary: Pedestrian tunnels under Rivers Street where students are permitted to use spray paint for creative expression and announcements.
cards.evidence_claim: The expression tunnels under Rivers Street are the only place at Appalachian State where graffiti and other forms of art and vandalism are not only allowed, but encouraged.
cards.access_notes: Accessible 24/7 via pedestrian paths under Rivers Street near Rankin Science Hall.

cards.title: Visit the Unofficial Mascots
cards.subtitle: Campus Wildlife Retreat
cards.notes: Relax by the water and watch the resident ducks, often called the university's unofficial mascots. It's a peaceful spot for a quick break between classes on the west side of campus.
cards.short_summary: A scenic campus pond and park area home to a variety of domesticated ducks and a popular spot for student relaxation.
cards.evidence_claim: The ducks at Appalachian State University have been referred to as “the best unofficial mascots in college” and provide joy to everyone who visits them at the Duck Pond.
cards.access_notes: Public park area accessible 24/7. Located near the Rivers Street Parking Deck.

cards.title: Picnic by Boone Creek
cards.subtitle: Secluded Campus Green
cards.notes: Find a quiet spot in this often-overlooked park featuring a gazebo and the flowing Boone Creek. Ideal for a peaceful picnic or reading away from the busier Sanford Mall.
cards.short_summary: A tranquil, wooded park on campus featuring a creek, walking paths, and a gazebo.
cards.evidence_claim: Durham Park is located off Blowing Rock Road... It includes a portion of Boone Creek... the park offers a calm space for whatever one may need it for.
cards.source_title: OPINION: Beauty in simplicity: App State's underrated park
cards.access_notes: Open 24/7; located between University Drive and Rivers Street.

cards.title: Relax in the Indoor Garden
cards.subtitle: Plemmons Student Union
cards.notes: Warm up during winter in this glass-enclosed space featuring tropical plants and water fountains. It's a favorite indoor hang for students looking for natural light and quiet study.
cards.short_summary: A sun-filled indoor garden and lounge area within the student union, perfect for year-round relaxation.
cards.evidence_claim: The addition, known as the Summit Trail Solarium, features a passive-solar, south-facing garden environment, ambient water fountains, and sky-lit reading areas.
cards.source_title: Appalachian State University – Plemmons Student Union Solarium
cards.access_notes: Open during Plemmons Student Union hours: Mon-Fri 7am-11pm, Sat 10am-6pm, Sun 3pm-11pm.

cards.title: View Boone from the Skybridge
cards.subtitle: Panoramic Mountain Overlook
cards.notes: Walk the new ADA-accessible skybridge for a 1,000-foot-high view of the campus and town. It's a short drive or steep hike from downtown and offers free admission.
cards.short_summary: A county park overlooking Boone featuring a newly renovated accessible skybridge with panoramic mountain views.
cards.evidence_claim: The centerpiece of the project is a new ADA-accessible skybridge overlook... Admission is free.
cards.source_title: Howard Knob County Park Reopens With New $2.2 Million Skybridge Overlook
cards.access_notes: Open May 1 - October 20, 8:30 am to 7:30 pm. Free admission.

cards.title: Walk the New River Greenway
cards.subtitle: Accessible Nature Path
cards.notes: Walk, run, or bike along this paved trail following the South Fork of the New River. It connects campus to local parks and features historic ruins and picnic shelters.
cards.short_summary: A multi-use paved trail system through Boone offering scenic river views and easy access to nature.
cards.evidence_claim: This fully accessible trail is either paved or gravel... It follows and crosses the South Fork of the New River through open meadows and colorful forests.
cards.access_notes: Open daily from dawn to dusk. Multiple trailheads available, including near State Farm Road.

cards.entity_name: Don Kennedy Trails at State Farm
cards.title: Run the Cross Country Trails
cards.subtitle: State Farm Fields
cards.notes: Train on the same four-mile trail system used by the university's cross country teams. These grass and dirt paths offer a soft surface for running along the river.
cards.short_summary: A dedicated cross country trail system at the State Farm Fields complex used for both team training and public recreation.
cards.evidence_claim: The Don Kennedy trails offer more than four miles of trails and courses sitting along the New River... home to the Appalachian men and women's cross country teams.
cards.source_title: Don Kennedy Trails at State Farm - Facilities
cards.access_notes: Open to the public for running and walking when not in use for university athletic events.
